tested:
── Generic-KVM fallback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
Used for any uploaded qcow2/vmdk that doesn't match a known vendor profile.
e1000 NICs + virtio disk + x86_64 are the safest defaults for unknown VMs
(they work with most OS images without needing paravirtual drivers).
── Linux cloud images (cloud-init NoCloud day-0) ───────────────────────────
2026-08-20 (Wave 3, LLA-064): the catalog's "ubuntu-server"/"debian" entries install
upstream *cloudimg* builds - no loginable account until cloud-init provisions one, so
these MUST carry day0_channel="cloud-init" (see day0_channels.LinuxCloudInitChannel).
Curated here (rather than on generic-vm) so the cidata ISO is only ever attached to an
image family known to read it - generic-vm is also the fallback base for every
registry-imported NOS without a curated profile. Serial console (cloud images boot
with console=ttyS0), virtio NIC/disk (the registry's own values for these images).

reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
boot_timeout_sec 180 -> 400 (2026-09-12, Wave 21 close): live-reproduced 3/3 on
the registered "ubuntu-22.04" image - node-manager's own day0 logs show
cloud-init's "ready marker confirmed" line never lands within 180s of node
start (a sibling cloud image needed 274s for the SAME cloud-init channel/marker
mechanism to confirm, and that one had enough budget to still pass) - the login
prompt is real and un-injected (NPX-1040/1039 both working correctly), root's
password simply hasn't been seeded by cloud-init yet when apply_config_serial's
180s deadline runs out. Same class of inconsistency-with-a-documented-sibling
gap NPX-1033 already fixed for "vios"/"iosv" - 400s matches that fix's own value.
